_howto: Newest first. Add an entry at the top each time you push an update; the website reads this file. tag: new | improved | fixed. Keep it in step with CHANGELOG.md, written for players instead of developers.

items.text: Every week, Monday to Sunday, the three fastest athletes at each distance take gold, silver and bronze. Your best online time of the week is the one that counts.
World Records now opens on This Week: the running standings, with the top three holding the medal spots and a countdown to the end of the week.
Last week's medallists are shown beside the board, and you get an announcement on the title screen when you win one.
Hall of Fame: every weekly medal ever awarded, browsable by month, plus the all-time medal table.
Your career page shows your gold, silver and bronze count.
Keyboard and phone each have their own medals, as they do their own records.
In a race room on your phone, tap INVITE to open the share sheet and text a friend a link to the room.
On a computer, press I in the room to copy the invite, then paste it into any message.
Opening an invite link takes a signed-in athlete straight into the room. New players sign in first, then land in it.
Phones and tablets can now play with their on-screen keyboard. Tap TYPE to open it; the text to type appears in large letters just above the keyboard.
On-screen buttons for the menus: arrows, Enter and Esc.
Every result is marked as typed on a keyboard or a phone. World Records keeps separate boards for each; up and down arrows switch between them.
Phone and keyboard players can still race each other in the same room.
In the race room, the host's start press could occasionally be missed. It now always registers.
Hold your phone upright for the best view: sideways leaves very little room above the keyboard.
The rival's portrait no longer covers part of the result screen after a race. Portraits still show when you choose who to race.
Every nationality has a pixel flag, 70 in all, drawn in the game's own style.
On the track, your flag flies above your athlete and sits beside your name on the scoreboard. Online, each opponent carries theirs.
Flags also show when you pick your nationality, on the title screen, in the race room and on World Records.
Compete: host a race and share the five-digit room PIN, or join a friend's. Up to four athletes start on the same gun.
The host picks the distance and can change it between races. Everyone stays in the room for the next one.
Results are worked out by the server from each athlete's keystrokes, so a time cannot simply be claimed.
World Records: the fastest times ever at each distance, the top typing speeds and the most race wins, from online races.
Going online uses the same name, nationality and PIN as your athlete, and the same PIN signs you in from any computer.
The 200m, 400m, 800m and 1500m are open in Train, alongside the 100m. One character is one metre at every distance.
Longer races scroll the text two lines at a time, so you always see what is coming next.
Every distance has its own best time, ghost, rival ladder and Meet Champion badge.
The career page covers all five distances. Left and right arrows switch between them.
Time standards for each distance are set at the same typing speeds as the 100m: 60, 80, 100 and 120 words a minute.

notes.title: The main menu, rivals and your career

items.text: Main menu: Train, Compete, Career and World Records. Up and down arrows to choose, Enter to go.
Train: pick a distance, then race. The 100m is open; the 200m, 400m, 800m and 1500m are listed and on the way.
Rivals: after picking a distance, race one of ten opponents, from Terry Shellman the Turtle (under 25 words a minute) to The Peregrine (110 and up). Each one unlocks when you beat the one before.
Rivals play by your rules: they type the same line, make mistakes and stumble like you do. Beat all ten to earn the Meet Champion badge on your career page.
Every rival has a portrait, shown when you choose who to race and when the result comes in.
Time trial is still there: race the ghost of your own best run.
Career page: your best time and words per minute, recent averages, accuracy, reaction time, clean races, false starts and your recent races.
Every finished race is now kept in your history, so your career figures build as you play.
Compete and World Records show what is coming: hosted races for up to four athletes that you join with a room PIN, and all-time leaderboards.
New start-screen art, with the menu now live on top of it.
The Typlympics logo is in the header of this page.

notes.title: Sign in and the real start screen

items.text: Athlete sign-in, arcade style: enter your name, pick your nationality and set a four-digit PIN. Your record is waiting next time you type your name and PIN.
Several athletes can share one computer, each with their own best times. Type GUEST to play without a PIN.
The hand-made start screen is in the game and on this page. Menu rows for modes that are not built yet are dimmed.
Your name and nationality show on the scoreboard during a race.
Best times from earlier builds are kept under the GUEST athlete.
This website: play in the page or full screen, see what is coming, and read these notes.
The game now publishes itself here every time the code is updated.
Drive phase: your athlete stays low for the first five metres, then rises into full stride.
Finish dip at the line, dust at your feet on every stride, and speed lines after 15 clean keys in a row.
Photo finish: end within a tenth of a second of your best and the margin is shown to the millisecond.
Tested on QWERTY, Dvorak, Colemak, AZERTY and QWERTZ layouts. The game reads the character you type, not the physical key.
Held keys, paste and keyboard shortcuts can never move your athlete, and key times are checked to the millisecond.
100m sprint: 100 characters, one metre each. The hundredth correct key stops the clock.
Start sequence with a random gun delay and a false start rule.
A wrong key makes you stumble for a fifth of a second. No backspace needed.
Result screen with your time, the gap to your best, splits at 30, 60 and 100 metres, reaction time, words per minute and accuracy.
Your best run is saved on your device and races beside you as a ghost.
A fresh line of text every race, balanced so times on different lines are comparable.
